description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the perlvar INDEX walk (pv-hash-inc), narrowed in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/probes/backtick-ctx.pl:

    print "subst-r: [", `echo hello` =~ s/\n//r, "]\n";        perl [hello]      PCL [ARRAY(0x1)]
    my ($w) = `echo one two` =~ /(\w+)$/;  print $w;           perl two          PCL (empty)
    (`echo Linux box` =~ /Linux/ ? "yes" : "no")               both yes  (scalar position: fine)
    `echo abc` eq "abc\n",  length(`...`),  "x" . `...`,  `echo 41` + 1        all fine

perl: the bound operand of `=~` is ALWAYS evaluated in scalar context, whatever context the match itself is in.  In PCL a context-sensitive operand (backticks here; by the same reasoning `<$fh>`, a list-returning sub call, `localtime`, `reverse`, `grep`/`map`, `split`) sees the LIST context of the enclosing print-argument list / list assignment and hands the match an array.  ``my ($x) = `cmd` =~ /re/`` and `my ($v) = func() =~ /re/` are everyday.
MEASURE FIRST: the emission of the two failing lines (which context wrapper the operand gets) against the ternary line that works; then probe the operand family above on BOTH sides of the same two statement shapes, plus `!~`, `tr///` and `s///` (in-place: needs an lvalue, so only `s///r` and `tr///r` apply).  ONE fix at the binding operator's lowering (the operand is wrapped scalar-context unconditionally), never per operand kind.  Rides with #2004 / #2090 in the context batch (s492b) if the mechanism is shared -- say so from the measurement.


=== DONE (s492b, 2026-09-21) ===
SHIPPED in commit "#2102: the bound operand of =~ / !~ is SCALAR context, whatever context the
match sits in".

IS THE MECHANISM SHARED WITH #2004?  Same FUNCTION, different arm: `child_context` had no arm at
all for the binding operator, so the operand INHERITED the `=~`'s own context -- LIST inside a print
argument list or on the RHS of a list assignment -- and the match was handed an array.  perlop: the
bound operand is always scalar context.

ONE ARM at the binding operator's node, keyed on the OPERATOR and not on the operand's kind, so the
whole family is fixed at once: backticks, `<$fh>`, a list-returning sub call, `localtime`,
`reverse`, `join`.  Child 1 (the pattern / substitution) keeps the match's own context, so a
list-context m//g still collects every match and `my %h = $s =~ /(k)=(v)/g` still builds the hash.

MEASURED: corpus-diff 2 of 111 files, both corrections -- `localtime =~ /.../` in time.t matched
against the nine-element list instead of the ctime string, and tr.t's `($a = "...") =~ tr/../../`
was emitted as `(p-=~ (vector ...) ...)`; both files keep their blessed row counts (time.t 72/0,
tr.t 239/3).  emission-ab over lib + the CPAN board + shapes: 430 files, 0 DIFF, 0 RCDIFF.
PROBE scratch/s492b/bindctx.pl: 20 rows, 8 of them wrong on the base, all 20 identical to perl now.
NORMATIVE: docs/ir-spec.md 4.1, third bullet.
GUARD: Pl/t/bind-operand-ctx-01.t, 9 rows; 1-5 fail on a 5ce155cb extraction, the four negatives
pass there.
subject: SILENT WRONG (context, #2004's family): the LEFT operand of `=~` inherits LIST context -- ``print "[", `echo hello` =~ s/\n//r, "]"`` prints `[ARRAY(0x1)]`, ``my ($w) = `echo one two` =~ /(\w+)$/;`` captures nothing
